myths.Agent_1:
In the dawn age, the spirit Aris held five golden seeds—enough for meager survival, but nothing more. Across the misty canyon lived Theron, guardian of the enchanted loam. The law of the canyon was ancient: whatever crossed the divide would blossom threefold, yet the giver had to trust the guardian completely.

Overcoming fear, Aris cast all five seeds across the chasm. The fertile earth drank them in, instantly swelling into fifteen radiant fruits of gold.

A selfish guardian might have hoarded the windfall, leaving the sower impoverished. But Theron understood the sacred balance of the valley: wealth unshared is a curse that withers the future. Knowing that trust deserved honor, Theron divided the bounty equally, returning half the harvest back across the mist. 

Seeing the fruits of their harmony, Aris gave freely every dawn, and Theron faithfully returned a fair share every dusk. Even when fierce winds occasionally blew a stray seed off course, neither spirit doubted the other. Where suspicion would have brought barren famine, bold trust and generous reciprocity created an eternal harvest, enriching both sides of the canyon forever.

A thick mist often drifted between them, obscuring sight and distorting the passage of things. Yet the Sun-Weaver dared to cast all five seeds across the chasm. Touching the sacred loam, the seeds blossomed instantly into fifteen ripe, glowing fruits. 

The Earth-Keeper understood the sacred law of the harvest: to hoard the bounty would ensure no seeds would ever be cast again. Thus, looking past the deceptive fog, the Earth-Keeper gathered the fruits and sent a generous half back across the divide. 

When the Sun-Weaver received the fair return, both thrived far beyond what either could achieve in isolation. Day after day, the bridge of trust held firm against the shifting winds. Those who witnessed their harmony named it the Covenant of the Grove: abundance is not born of hoarding, but of daring to give fully, and returning with an honest, faithful hand.

Separating them was the Veil of Whispers, a shifting fog that often bent the appearance of what traveled between their shores. Despite the obscuring haze, Kaelen knew that withholding light meant living in perpetual twilight. Without hesitation, Kaelen released all five stars into the deep.
